Arithmetic and comparison operators for expressions

Source: R/operators.R
opt_operators.Rd

Expressions support +, -, *, / and ^ elementwise, with numeric vectors, matrices and other expressions of the same model. Only length-one operands are recycled; other length mismatches are errors. The comparisons <=, >= and == build constraint relations for opt_constraint(); they never return TRUE or FALSE. Strict inequalities < and > and != are rejected because they do not define closed feasible sets. Logical operators are not overloaded; R's && and || cannot be overloaded at all, and logical constraints between expressions are not supported.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'opt_expr'
Ops(e1, e2)

# S3 method for class 'opt_expr'
Math(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'opt_expr'
Summary(..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'opt_expr'
mean(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'opt_expr'
matrixOps(x, y)

# S4 method for class 'Matrix,opt_expr'
x %*% y

# S4 method for class 'opt_expr,Matrix'
x %*% y

Arguments

e1, e2

Expressions or numeric values.

x

An expression.

...

For log(), an optional base; otherwise unused.

na.rm

Ignored; expressions have no missing values.

y

An expression or numeric matrix.

Value

An opt_expr for arithmetic, an opt_relation for comparisons.

Examples

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2)
2 * x + 1
#> <opt_expr 2, affine>
#>   [1] 2*x[1] + 1
#>   [2] 2*x[2] + 1
sum(x^2)
#> <opt_expr 1, quadratic>
#>   x[1]^2 + x[2]^2 
x[1] + x[2] <= 4
#> <opt_relation: 1 row, affine <= 0>
#>   x[1] + x[2] <= 4
